description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Arian Smith is expected to miss time with a knee injury.
items.impact: It is unclear how serious the injury is for Smith.
items.title: Arian Smith (knee) expected to miss time

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said Brian Burns sustained a low ankle sprain in Week 2 against the Rams.
items.impact: Burns suffered the sprain in the fourth quarter of Monday's blowout loss. He was diagnosed with a low ankle sprain. His status is uncertain for Week 3.
items.title: Brian Burns suffers low ankle sprain

items.author: Ari Koslow
items.desc: Rams head coach Sean McVay said he's "not sure" if Puka Nacua will play in Week 3.
items.impact: McVay said he's "hopeful" Nacua will be able to suit up against Denver next week. If he remains sidelined, Davante Adams and Terrance Ferguson would remain in bigger roles.
items.title: Puka Nacua (hip) uncertain for Week 3

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.desc: Malik Nabers (shoulder) has returned to the Giants game against the Rams on Monday.
items.impact: Nabers was initially questionable to return with a shoulder injury that appeared to put him in a lot of pain. However, it seems to be just a stinger, and he's back on the field. It's worth keeping an eye on though, as another hit could put him right back out.
items.title: Malik Nabers (shoulder) returns to Monday Night Football

items.author: Nate Miller
items.desc: Will Johnson (neck) could miss the remainder of the season.
items.impact: Johnson went down with a neck injury during Sunday's loss to the Seahawks. The second-year corner has already recorded eight tackles and a fumble recovery in two games this season. Kei'Trel Clark will likely see a significant boost in playing time with Johnson down.
items.title: Will Johnson (neck) could miss rest of season

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: The Giants' D/ST logged one sack, one interception, and one fumble recovery while allowing 28 points in Monday night's loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: New York's defense struggled on Monday night. They allowed 28 points over the course of the game, despite actually forcing a couple turnovers to help their offense out. This unit should not be started moving forward, even with a relatively easy schedule coming down the pipe for them.
items.title: Giants D/ST allows 28 points in loss Monday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Dominic Zvada made both of his field-goal attempts in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: Zvada scored New York's only points on Monday night, accounting for all six of their points with his two made field goals. He has looked pretty good through the first two games of the season, although he doesn't project to be a good fantasy option at the position anytime soon.
items.title: Dominic Zvada scores six points in loss Monday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Tyrone Tracy Jr. did not see a single carry or target in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: New York seems to have phased Tracy out of the offense altogether, as he was relegated to just special teams against the Rams and saw no opportunities on offense. Najee Harris worked in and saw four touches on the night, so it looks like the 26-year old may have lost his spot as a depth piece in the backfield.
items.title: Tyrone Tracy Jr. held without a touch Monday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Najee Harris rushed the ball four times for six yards in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: Harris wasn't able to accomplish anything on the box score on Monday night, but it looks like he is starting to get involved on New York's offense. He saw the second-most carries out of anyone on the team, although he wasn't able to do much with them. It looks like he may be overtaking Tyrone Tracy Jr. in this backfield, who himself didn't see a single opportunity on offense against the Rams.
items.title: Najee Harris sees four carries in loss Monday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Darnell Mooney hauled in 2-of-3 targets for 48 yards in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: The veteran was technically the team's leader in receiving yards on Monday night, but he did it with just 48 over the course of the game, which still left him with a poor fantasy total. He shouldn't be rostered in most league formats for the foreseeable future.
items.title: Darnell Mooney leads team in receiving Monday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Devin Singletary rushed the ball three times for nine yards and failed to catch his lone target in Monday's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: Singletary involvement was minimal on Monday, as he saw just three touches over the course of the game. He wasn't able to do much with those touches, and it was less than ideal to see Najee Harris come in and out-touch him in this matchup. He is off of the fantasy radar moving forward.
items.title: Devin Singletary a non-factor Monday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Malachi Fields hauled in 2-of-6 targets for 30 yards in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: The Giants were trying to get the rookie wideout the ball on Monday night, but he was only able to haul in two out of his six targets over the course of the game. He finished with just 30 yards and isn't expected to get much better over the next couple of weeks with QB Jaxson Dart (knee) seemingly set to miss some time for New York.
items.title: Malachi Fields hauls in two passes Monday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Jameis Winston completed 11-of-27 passing attempts for 111 yards and an interception in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: The veteran quarterback came into the game when Jaxson Dart left with a knee injury. Winston didn't look good against the Rams, finishing with just over 100 scoreless yards in a blowout loss. It looks like Jaxson Dart is going to miss a bit of time with a sprained MCL, leaving Winston as the short-term starter for New York, which will be less than ideal for most of the fantasy options on their roster.
items.title: Jameis Winston underwhelms in loss Monday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Isaiah Likely hauled in 5-of-10 targets for 33 yards in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: Likely didn't put up great numbers on Monday night, finishing with just 33 yards in a loss to the Rams. He was still the most targeted player on the team by far, however, which is a good sign that he will bounce back and return to form sometime in the near future. His bounce back may be delayed is Jaxson Dart (knee) has to miss time for the Giants.
items.title: Isaiah Likely hauls in five passes Monday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Cam Skattebo rushed the ball 12 times for 36 yards and caught four passes for 19 yards in Monday night's 28-6 loss to the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: Skattebo was pretty well bottled up on Monday night. He was only able to rush for 36 yards at an inefficient clip of 3.0 yards per carry, and he didn't add much in the passing game outside of four receptions. New York's offense as a whole was a mess with injuries in this game, but the young running back will have ample opportunities to bounce back with matchups against the Titans and Cardinals coming up over the next two weeks.
items.title: Cam Skattebo inefficient in loss Monday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: The Rams' D/ST logged two sacks and an interception while allowing just six points in Monday night's blowout win over the New York Giants.
items.impact: Los Angeles' defense looked good on Monday night. They held the Giants' offense to just six points on the night, but that was also aided by the multiple key injuries that New York suffered over the course of the night. This unit can be started in a matchup against the Broncos next week, although that is by no means an easy game for them.
items.title: Rams D/ST plays well in win Monday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Harrison Mevis went 4-for-4 on his extra-point attempts but missed his lone field-goal attempt in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
items.impact: Mevis missed a field goal late in Monday night's game, but luckily for him, it wasn't very consequential with Los Angeles already being up several scores. He should return to being a solid fantasy option at the position somewhat soon.
items.title: Harrison Mevis misses kick in win Monday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Tutu Atwell caught 1-of-2 targets for 19 yards in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
items.impact: The veteran wideout wasn't able to capitalize on the absence of Puka Nacua (hip) on Monday night, hauling in just one pass over the course of the night. He remains off of the fantasy radar for the foreseeable future.
items.title: Tutu Atwell held to one catch Monday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Colby Parkinson caught two passes for 15 yards in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
items.impact: Parkinson wasn't much of a factor on Monday night, totaling just 15 yards over the course of the team's blowout win. It seems that Terrance Ferguson is clearly surpassing him as a receiving threat, which would render Parkinson entirely irrelevant from a fantasy standpoint moving forward.
items.title: Colby Parkinson quiet in win Monday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Terrance Ferguson caught 6-of-9 targets for 54 yards and a touchdown in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
items.impact: Ferguson looked great on Monday night. He saw more work than usual with Puka Nacua (hip) out of the lineup for Los Angeles, and he was able to capitalize by putting up 54 yards and scoring a touchdown against the Giants. He has shown his talent and could continue to have week-to-week upside moving forward, although good games will be hard to predict when Nacua makes his return to the lineup.
items.title: Terrance Ferguson plays well in win Monday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Blake Corum rushed the ball 12 times for 79 yards and caught one pass for 13 yards in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
items.impact: Los Angeles' offense looked great on Monday night, and Corum was no exception to that. He put up 92 total yards on just 13 opportunities, although he wasn't able to get into the endzone to put the capstone on that. The Rams' backfield is a situation to continue monitoring, with Corum and Kyren Williams each seeing the same amount of carries in this blowout win.
items.title: Blake Corum totals 92 yards in win Monday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Davante Adams hauled in 8-of-10 targets for 195 yards and two touchdowns in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
items.impact: Adams had one of his best games as a Ram on Monday night. He put up nearly 200 receiving yards in this blowout win over the Giants, and he was also able to get into the end zone on two separate occasions. He really stepped up in the absence of Puka Nacua (hip), so if he misses more time, fantasy managers should continue to view Adams as a can't-miss option any given week that he's the team's undisputed WR1.
items.title: Davante Adams dominant in win Monday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Kyren Williams rushed the ball 12 times for 85 yards and caught two passes for 12 yards and a touchdown in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
items.impact: Williams had a productive night on Monday. He led the team in rushing and fell just three yards shy of the 100-total yards mark over the course of the game, and he was also able to haul in a touchdown to put the cherry on top. Concerns still exist for his season-long outlook, though, with Blake Corum seeing just one less touch on the night and seemingly only getting better and better.
items.title: Kyren Williams finds end zone Monday

items.author: Leo Sells
items.desc: Matthew Stafford completed 22-of-31 passing attempts for 327 yards, four touchdowns, and one interception in Monday night's 28-6 win over the New York Giants.
items.impact: The reigning MVP had a great bounce-back game on Monday night after a disappointing season opener last week. He scored four touchdowns against the Giants and limited his mistakes overall, helping lead Los Angeles to a blowout win over New York. The only questions for him moving forward will be consistency and the health of his wideouts, with Puka Nacua (hip) currently out of the lineup for the Rams.
items.title: Matthew Stafford tosses four touchdowns in win Monday
